property_summary: The state variable pastBlockTime must be strictly monotonic and cannot skip ahead by more than 1 on any call.
After any call to fallback, either the call reverted with insufficient value or the new pastBlockTime equals the previous pastBlockTime value plus the change in block timestamp.
When a call to fallback succeeds and does not trigger a transfer (block.number % 15 != 0), the pastBlockTime must equal the block.timestamp at call time, not block.timestamp + 1.
After calling fallback with exactly 10 ether, if the block number is not divisible by 15, then pastBlockTime increases.
After a successful fallback call with exactly 10 ether, pastBlockTime equals the block.timestamp of that call.
After any interaction, pastBlockTime always equals block.timestamp of the last call that reverted or succeeded (or 0 if none).
After any call to the fallback function with msg.value = 10 ether, pastBlockTime is updated to block.timestamp regardless of whether the if block executes.
After a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether that sets pastBlockTime, the value of pastBlockTime remains unchanged after a second call that does not meet the time requirement.
After a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, pastBlockTime equals the block.timestamp at the end of that call.
After a fallback call that sends exactly 10 ether, pastBlockTime is always updated even if the transfer reverts.
After a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, if the if block does not execute (i.e., block.number % 15 != 0), pastBlockTime is updated to block.timestamp.
The contract's balance after any interaction is always zero (or not zero) depending on whether block.number % 15 == 0 when the caller sends exactly the required value.
The fallback can only succeed when msg.value is exactly 10 ether.
If block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's balance after the fallback call must be zero; otherwise it must be 10 ether.
If the fallback call succeeds and the block number modulo 15 equals 0, the contract balance must be 0; otherwise the balance must be 10 ether.
The contract's balance after a successful fallback call is zero if and only if block.number % 15 == 0.
After any call to the fallback with msg.value = 10 ether and block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, the contract's balance should decrease when block.number % 15 == 0.
After a call to the fallback function with exactly 10 ether, the value of pastBlockTime should always increase relative to its previous value.
After a call to the fallback function with 10 ether at a time when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime and block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's balance decreases by exactly 10 ether.
After a successful fallback call with 10 ether when block.number % 15 == 0, the contract's balance must decrease by at least 1 wei (i.e., the transfer must occur).
If the block number is a multiple of 15, the contract balance after the fallback call equals the initial balance minus 10 ether; otherwise, the balance stays the same.
After any payable call to the fallback with exactly 10 ether, the contract's balance remains unchanged if the condition block.number % 15 != 0.
After calling fallback with exactly 10 ether when block.number % 15 != 0, the call does not revert on C (reference) but reverts on the mutated version.
